analysis.title: The Taiwan Massacre
key_insights: EWT has fallen 34% from its all-time highs and trades well below its 200-day moving average. Foreign selling continues and positioning has been cut sharply.

A month earlier The Market Ear flagged crowded AI positioning, accelerating foreign outflows and stretched divergences versus Korea and semiconductors. Fundamentals were strong but expectations were extreme.
EWT has closed its gap versus EWY, a reset the note calls absolutely massive.
The EWT December 95 put flagged less than a month ago rose from about $2 to almost $20, nearly 10x.
Foreign investors sold another $6bn of Taiwan equities last week. Cumulative foreign net selling is $99bn YTD per Goldman, of which $75bn is TSMC.

Hedge funds cut Taiwan exposure month to date through long liquidation and fresh shorts. Net allocation is 4.4% (24th percentile over one year, 85th over five years) and gross allocation is 3.8% (89th percentile over five years).

Taiwan is the biggest underweight among both Asian and global EM active funds: Asian funds are 530bps underweight and EM funds 425bps underweight per Goldman. Both groups reduced exposure further in October.
The usual Q4 to Chinese New Year seasonal strength in Taiwan has not appeared, as the AI unwind continues.

Weekly EWT RSI has fallen faster than at any point since the Covid crash, though it has not reached outright disaster levels. The authors are not ready to catch falling knives yet but say some extremes are hard to ignore.

sector_views.rationale: Foreign outflows, hedge fund de-risking and a 34% drawdown in EWT from highs. The note says it is not ready to buy the dip yet.
